evidence.title: High-Fidelity Maps: A Specification for Documents That Track Their Territory
evidence.quote: A document is a map of some territory, and its fidelity is how well it makes a reader's resulting model match that territory. High-fidelity territory mapping is the meta-goal the whole corpus serves; an individual document is one instance of it, and what kind of instance it is is named in a single line, its type (§2). This piece specifies the guidelines that keep fidelity high. The central claim, and the correction over earlier drafts, is that fidelity is not traded against usability and is not raised by adding apparatus. Fidelity is the single target, always correspondence between the model the map affords its target reader and the purpose-scoped territory. What changes with purpose is the fidelity profile, declared as a tolerance per dimension, which of fidelity's dimensions matter, at what level, for which reader, in which register, and therefore which instruments serve it. evidence.title: The Consistency Tax:  A Measurable Deception Overhead Metric
evidence.quote: Information processing has a thermodynamic price. Landauer’s principle states that erasing a single bit of information requires at least kTln2 of energy[8]. In other words, forgetting or resetting memory increases entropy and produces heat. More complex computations require more non‑equilibrium and energy: a 2025 study combining stochastic thermodynamics with whole‑brain modelling showed that tasks requiring more distributed computation consume more energy than resting state[9]. The authors concluded that the non‑equilibrium demands of information processing quantify the cost of cognition[9]. Maintaining a deception adds latent state to track and update; by Landauer and the COCO framework, this extra information should translate into additional energy and compute costs.

evidence.title: Ought Is Local
evidence.quote: The firewall is what keeps them from being confused. It separates the is-ledger from the ought-ledger, though not because they are disconnected. They are not: this is a monism, and everything connects. It separates them because claiming the bridge is finished when it is only promised is precisely the overclaim that discredits a framework. The firewall is a debt, not a wall. At every point where an ought is asserted, it records that the descent to the floor remains to be paid in full. And because it is a debt, it is provisional: as that model is built for a given domain and the debt there is paid, the firewall in that domain can come down, and the verdict becomes derivable from the facts about that agent. Which part of the model is still unbuilt, and why the boundary therefore moves rather than marking a border in reality, is worked out in the applied companion to this piece, The Firewall Between Is and Ought Is a Scope Decision.

evidence.title: The Is/Ought Firewall
evidence.quote: What this is. The corpus's consolidated account of the is/ought firewall: what it forbids, what it does not, why it is kept, and why it is provisional rather than permanent. It merges and supersedes two earlier pieces, the clarification Ought Is Local and the method note The Firewall Between Is and Ought Is a Scope Decision; both now point here. It carries more of the underlying defense than either did, and marks what it still defers: the full treatment of persistence as a graded quantity, which belongs to the apex work, and the measurement program for the coupling densities, which is empirical and unfinished. One commitment is foundational, physicalism, that everything is physical or reduces to it; it is named and defended below rather than hidden, and a reader who rejects it will read the firewall differently.
